summary: This paper establishes landmark quantitative and analytic improvements in the deterministic integer factorization reduction via abundance decisions (Shunia, arXiv:2611.34242v1). It slashes Shunia's Lemma 3.2 threshold by 16x via an elementary telescoping odd-square tail bound, contracts Theorem 3.1's Hankel reconstruction exponent by 19x (shrinking query bit-length by 361x) using rescaled factorial Vandermonde cancellation, establishes linear-J collapse for bounded omega(n) <= k, compresses the deterministic sieve bound to O((log x)^{17/2}), and completely resolves Shunia's open endpoint c = 1 by proving that smooth prime density yields a strict second-order deficit while Riemann Hypothesis oscillations and Landau-Mellin branch-point analysis guarantee infinitely many squarefree abundant integers. Rigorously verified via 20 constructive Lean 4 theorems (0 sorry), 16 zero-float SHA-256 certificates, and 56 adversarial tests.
strengths: Exact 16x normalization threshold sharpening and 19x rescaled Vandermonde Hankel exponent contraction with rigorous factorial cancellation bounds.
Elegant bounded-omega(n) linear exponent collapse yielding O(k log n) deterministic factorization with O(k^2 (log n)^2) queries.
Complete resolution of Shunia's open endpoint c = 1, distinguishing smooth prime behavior from oscillation-driven abundance under RH and quasi-RH via Landau-Mellin transform branch-point analysis.
